questions.question: In single-head attention, what are Q, K, and V?
options: Query, Key, and Value projections of the input
The three layers of an LSTM
questions.explanation: Q (query), K (key), and V (value) are linear projections of the input. The query asks 'what am I looking for?', the key says 'what do I contain?', and the value is what gets returned when a key matches a query.

questions.question: What does 'multi-head' mean in multi-head attention?
options: Running several independent attention functions in parallel, each with different projections
Attending to multiple sequence positions at once
questions.explanation: Multi-head attention runs h independent attention heads in parallel, each with its own Q/K/V projection matrices. Each head can learn to attend to different aspects of the input (syntax, semantics, position, etc.).

questions.question: If the model dimension is d_model=512 and there are 8 heads, what is the dimension per head?
questions.explanation: Each head operates on d_model / num_heads = 512 / 8 = 64 dimensions. The heads are run in parallel and their outputs are concatenated back to d_model before a final linear projection.

questions.question: Why do we scale the dot product by 1/√d_k before applying softmax?
options: To make the model train faster
Because large dot products push softmax into saturation regions with tiny gradients
To normalize the output to sum to 1
questions.explanation: When d_k is large, dot products grow in magnitude, pushing softmax outputs toward 0 or 1 where gradients vanish. Scaling by 1/√d_k keeps the variance around 1, keeping softmax in a well-behaved gradient region.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the final linear projection after concatenating all attention heads?
options: To reduce the concatenated head outputs back to d_model and mix information across heads
questions.explanation: Concatenating h heads gives h × d_head = d_model dimensions, but each head operated independently. The final W_O projection allows the model to mix information across heads, creating a combined representation.
